claims.text: Conventional powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys typically produces porosity, uneven melt pools, and surface roughness.
Applying an in situ laser re-melting pass immediately after deposition of each layer can reduce porosity in powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components.
Applying an in situ laser re-melting pass can reduce surface irregularities in powder-bed-fused high-entropy-alloy components.
Reduced porosity and surface irregularities will improve dimensional precision.
Reduced porosity and improved layer bonding will improve mechanical integrity.
The proposed intervention re-exposes every deposited layer to a controlled laser pass to re-melt and homogenize the material.
The intervention should be conducted under an inert atmosphere such as argon.
Laser power, scan speed, and beam modulation can be tuned to obtain partial re-melting without excessively disturbing part geometry.
In situ laser re-melting will produce a more refined and homogenized grain structure at melted-solidified interfaces.
In situ laser re-melting will improve bonding between deposited layers.
Localized secondary melting facilitates healing of microvoids.
Localized secondary melting smooths the surface profile.
Rapid re-solidification after the secondary laser pass yields a more uniform microstructure with fewer defects.
Relative to powder bed fusion without re-melting, the intervention will lower porosity.
Relative to powder bed fusion without re-melting, the intervention will improve surface finish and agreement with design dimensions.
Relative to powder bed fusion without re-melting, the intervention will increase yield strength and ductility.
The intervention is expected to apply to laboratory-scale high-entropy-alloy parts made by powder bed fusion under controlled atmospheres.
Similar re-melting treatments have improved microstructural homogeneity in simpler alloys.
Poorly optimized re-melting parameters in high-entropy alloys may cause grain growth or phase segregation because of their complex phase behavior.
